message: Joanna, in addition to the December 1990 "Composition in the Eighties" *CCC* essay he cites, Fulkerson's other review essay that I know of is his December 1979 *CCC* "Four Philosophies of Composition," where he lists "Neo-Platonic" (Macrorie and Coles), "Neo-Aristotelian" (Corbett), "New Rhetoric" (i.e., Berthoff's approach, which he favors), and that favorite target of vilification, "Current-Traditional Rhetoric." I think Jenny's right that there are a number of similarities to Berlin's work; I also think there's a strong indication in Fulkerson's work that the privileging of literary-text-as-object over writing-as-teachable-and-learnable-process you describe is a holdover from positivist and New Critical notions of the static text as external and objectively knowable truth.
